title: The generating graph in the nerve of a free category
statement: Let $O$ be a small set and $Q$ a small directed graph on $O$, given by a set $Q(x,y)$ of edges for every $x,y\in O$. Loops, parallel edges and isolated vertices are allowed. Let $P(Q)$ be the small free category [def-nagata-category] with objects $O$, morphisms finite composable words of edges, empty words as identities and concatenation as composition. Write $NP(Q)$ for its ordinary simplicial nerve, whose $n$-simplices are strings of $n$ composable morphisms. Let $K(Q)\subseteq NP(Q)$ be the smallest simplicial subset [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] containing every vertex and the one-simplex of every single edge of $Q$. Then the inclusion $K(Q)\hookrightarrow NP(Q)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence in the realization sense of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. No nonemptiness or connectedness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Dwyer--Kan, Simplicial localizations of categories (1980), Section 2.8 and Proposition 2.9 at k=1, printed p.271 (PDF p.5); Section 2.1 defines free categories. No Stacks tag states this result.
